common_name: Guinevere Delphinium (Lavender-Mauve with White Bee Pacific Giant)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost, or sow in fall for cool climates; Guinevere is one of the original named strains in the classic Pacific Giant delphinium series, bearing soft lavender-mauve flowers with a contrasting white or pink-toned center.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun, staking tall flower spikes to protect them from wind and summer storms. Guinevere produces towering spikes densely packed with large, semi-double, soft lavender-mauve to pink-tinted flowers, each centered with a contrasting 'bee,' opening from the bottom of the spike upward over several weeks in early summer, a softer pastel counterpart to the deep blues and purples of Pacific Giant siblings like King Arthur and Black Knight. In warm climates it is typically grown as a cool-season annual or short-lived biennial since it declines quickly in summer heat and humidity, while in cooler zones it can persist as a short-lived perennial with excellent drainage and protection from wind. All parts are toxic if ingested. Cut spent flower spikes back hard after the first bloom flush to encourage a possible secondary round of shorter spikes later in the season.
